correctness.rationale: From the published large-branch identity \(\theta=(y^3-y)/(y^4-2)\), setting \(r=y^2>\sqrt2\) gives \(\theta y^3=2+(r-2)^2(r+1)/(r^2-2)\ge2\), sharply at \(r=2\). The two nontrivial transition eigenvalues are then compared by exact positive numerator identities, yielding \(|\lambda_1|\le\lambda_2\) for \(0<\theta<1\). Hence the second-largest absolute eigenvalue is \(\lambda_2\le1/3\) and \(3\lambda_2^2-1\le-2/3\). The equality point gives \(y=\sqrt2\) and \(\theta=1/\sqrt2\).
